dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The natural-number-valued PMF obtained from a Boolean Bernoulli PMF by mapping true to 1 and false to 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the PMF whose masses at 0, 1, and all other natural numbers are characterized by the first three conclusions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real-valued PMF obtained from a Boolean Bernoulli PMF by mapping true to 1 and false to 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its induced measure is used in the expectation and centered-second-moment conclusions.

conclusions: The natural-number-valued 0–1 Bernoulli PMF has mass p at 1.
The natural-number-valued 0–1 Bernoulli PMF has mass 1 − p at 0.
For every natural number k distinct from 0 and 1, the natural-number-valued 0–1 Bernoulli PMF has mass zero at k.
The expectation of the real-valued 0–1 Bernoulli random variable is p.
The centered second moment of the real-valued 0–1 Bernoulli random variable about p is p(1 − p).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 p hp is the pushforward of the Boolean Bernoulli(p) PMF under the map true ↦ 1 and false ↦ 0, with values in Nat.
LocalDef002 p hp is the pushforward of the Boolean Bernoulli(p) PMF under the map true ↦ 1 and false ↦ 0, with values in Real.
PMF values are ENNReal-valued, while the expectation and centered-second-moment identities are Real-valued integrals against the measure induced by LocalDef002 p hp.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonnegative real p at most 1, the associated 0–1 Bernoulli distribution assigns probability p to 1, probability 1 − p to 0, and zero probability to every other natural number; its real-valued version has expectation p and centered second moment p(1 − p).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The mass values in the first three conclusions lie in ENNReal, so p is embedded into ENNReal there.
The mass at zero uses ENNReal subtraction. Because the hypothesis gives p ≤ 1, this agrees with the intended ordinary nonnegative difference 1 − p.
The final two conclusions use Real-valued integration against the measure induced by the real-valued PMF.
The target states the centered second-moment formula directly rather than introducing a named variance operation.
No material vacuity risk is present: p ranges over the nonempty interval [0,1], and the support assertion genuinely constrains every natural k other than 0 and 1.
